title: Admission Brochure
content: # Admission Brochure B.Tech admission is completed through online registration, entrance score submission, document upload, counselling, seat allotment, fee payment, and physical verification. ## Eligibility Criteria Admission to B.Tech programs requires passing Class XII (10+2) with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics as compulsory subjects and a minimum aggregate of 60 percent marks. Admission is based on the entrance exam rank and the counselling process. Diploma holders can take lateral entry into the second year of B.Tech programs based on their diploma marks and seat availability. ## Required Documents Required documents include Class X marksheet, Class XII marksheet, entrance scorecard, migration certificate, character certificate, category certificate if applicable, Aadhaar card, and passport-size photographs. Original documents are verified at the time of physical document verification after seat allotment. Two sets of photocopies are required for the admission file. ## Counselling Process After the

Two sets of photocopies are required for the admission file. ## Counselling Process After the entrance results, students register for counselling and fill their choice of branches in order of preference. Seats are allotted based on rank and category quota. Students must confirm the allotted seat within the deadline by paying the seat acceptance fee. If a student misses a counselling round, they can participate in the next round as long as seats are available. ## Key Dates Application forms open in the first week of April. The application deadline is the end of May. Entrance results are announced in June, followed by counselling rounds in July. Classes for the academic session begin in the first week of August. Fee payment must be completed before the start of the session. ## Quota and Reservation Seats are reserved as per government norms: 15 percent for Scheduled Caste, 7.5 percent for Scheduled Tribe, 27 percent for Other Backward Classes, and 10 percent for Economically Weaker Sections. Category certificates issued by the competent authority must be uploaded during registration and verified during document verification.

title: Complaint Services
content: # Complaint Registration Process ## How to Register a Complaint Students can register complaints through the college portal under the complaints section, or through the student services mobile app. Walk-in complaints are accepted at the student helpdesk counter in the administrative block from 10 AM to 5 PM on working days. Every complaint gets a unique complaint ID that is used to track the status. ## Complaint Categories Complaints are grouped into categories: academics, hostel, mess and food, fees and finance, infrastructure, library, transport, security, harassment, and others. Students must select the correct category so the complaint reaches the right department. Misrouted complaints are forwarded by the helpdesk within one working day. ## What Information to Provide For a good complaint, students should select a category, describe the issue clearly with dates and times, add location details like building and

content: working day. ## What Information to Provide For a good complaint, students should select a category, describe the issue clearly with dates and times, add location details like building and room number, and attach proof such as photos or receipts if available. Contact details are used by the concerned department to update the student about the resolution. ## Status Tracking The complaint status moves through these stages: submitted, assigned, under review, resolved, or escalated. Students receive updates through the portal and email at every stage change. If a complaint is not resolved within 7 working days, it is automatically escalated to the registrar office. ## Harassment and Safety Complaints Complaints related to harassment, ragging, or safety are handled by the internal complaints committee with confidentiality. title: Events Notices
content: # Events and Notices ## Tech Fest The annual technical festival TechNova is held in the second week of March. The fest includes coding competitions, robotics, hackathons, paper presentations, and workshops. Registration for events opens two weeks before the fest through the events portal. Students from all branches can participate and winning teams receive cash prizes and certificates. ## Cultural Fest The cultural fest Samvedna takes place in the first week of February. Events include dance, music, drama, fashion show, and literary competitions. Inter-college teams can participate with prior registration. The cultural committee announces the event schedule and audition dates through notices on the student portal and notice boards. ## Sports Meet The annual sports meet is held in January at the campus sports complex. title: Fee Structure
content: # Fee Structure ## Tuition Fees The tuition fee for B.Tech programs is Rs. 95,000 per year. The tuition fee for M.Tech programs is Rs. 80,000 per year. MBA program tuition fee is Rs. 1,20,000 per year. Fees can be paid online through the student portal using UPI, net banking, debit card, or credit card. An offline payment counter is available in the administrative block on working days from 10 AM to 4 PM. ## Other Charges A one-time admission fee of Rs. 5,000 is charged at the time of admission. The university registration fee is Rs. 3,000 per year. Caution money of Rs. 10,000 is refundable after completion of the program. The library and laboratory fee is Rs. 4,500 per year. The students welfare fund contribution is Rs. 500 per year. ## Hostel Fees Hostel fees for double sharing

title: Fee Structure
content: the program. The library and laboratory fee is Rs. 4,500 per year. The students welfare fund contribution is Rs. 500 per year. ## Hostel Fees Hostel fees for double sharing rooms are Rs. 60,000 per year and include lodging, mess charges, laundry, and Wi-Fi. Single room hostel fees are Rs. 85,000 per year. Hostel admission is separate from academic admission and must be applied for through the hostel portal. Hostel fees are non-refundable after the second week of the semester. ## Scholarships and Waivers Students belonging to reserved categories are eligible for government scholarship schemes through the National Scholarship Portal. Students scoring above 90 percent in the entrance exam receive a 25 percent tuition fee waiver. Merit-cum-means scholarships cover 50 percent of tuition fees for students with family income below Rs. 2.5 lakh per year. ## Late Fee and Refund

content: a 25 percent tuition fee waiver. Merit-cum-means scholarships cover 50 percent of tuition fees for students with family income below Rs. 2.5 lakh per year. ## Late Fee and Refund Policy A late fee of Rs. 500 per week applies if fees are not paid by the last date. If a student withdraws before the start of classes, the full tuition fee minus Rs. 5,000 is refunded. Withdrawal in the first two weeks of the semester gives a 50 percent refund. No refund is given for withdrawals after the first month of the semester.

title: Hostel Rules
content: # Hostel Rules ## Admission and Allotment Hostel admission is separate from academic admission. Students apply through the hostel portal and rooms are allotted on a first-come first-served basis. Boys and girls hostels are separate blocks with their own wardens and security. Students must complete hostel registration, pay the hostel fee, and collect their room keys from the warden office. Change of room requires written permission from the hostel warden. ## Timings and Entry Rules The hostel main gate closes at 10 PM on working days and at 11 PM on weekends. Students must sign the entry and exit register at the security desk. Latecomers must provide a valid reason and are reported to the warden. Visitors are allowed in the common room from 4 PM to 7 PM and must deposit their ID cards at the security desk. No

content: and are reported to the warden. Visitors are allowed in the common room from 4 PM to 7 PM and must deposit their ID cards at the security desk. No visitors are allowed in student rooms. ## Room Conduct Students are responsible for the furniture and fittings in their rooms. Damages are charged to the student account. Electrical appliances such as heaters, induction cookers, and kettles are not allowed in rooms. Cooking inside rooms is strictly prohibited. Students must keep rooms clean and maintain silence after 10 PM. ## Mess Rules The mess serves breakfast, lunch, evening snacks, and dinner. Mess timings are breakfast 7:30 to 9 AM, lunch 12:30 to 2 PM, snacks 5 to 6 PM, and dinner 8 to 9:30 PM. Mess menus are announced weekly. Students must register for meals on the mess app to reduce

title: Hostel Rules
content: to 2 PM, snacks 5 to 6 PM, and dinner 8 to 9:30 PM. Mess menus are announced weekly. Students must register for meals on the mess app to reduce food wastage. Special food requests during illness must be reported to the mess manager. ## Leave and Discipline Students going home must inform the warden and fill the leave register. An overnight leave requires parental consent through the hostel portal. Absence without permission for more than three days is reported to the parents. Ragging, smoking, alcohol, and drugs are strictly prohibited and are punishable with expulsion from the hostel and college. Repeated rule violations lead to a disciplinary committee review.

title: Library Timings

The library remains closed on Sundays and public holidays. The reading hall is open 24 hours during the examination period with the issue counter open from 8 AM to 8 PM. ## Services and Sections The library has separate sections for text books, reference books, journals, and digital resources. Book issue counter operates from 9 AM to 6 PM. Reference books, journals, and magazines are for in-library reading only and cannot be issued. title: Scholarship Details
content: # Scholarship Details ## Government Scholarships The college is registered on the National Scholarship Portal. Eligible students can apply for Post Matric Scholarships for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, and Other Backward Class students. The Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships covers 82,000 fresh scholarships every year for meritorious students. Students must apply on the National Scholarship Portal with their Aadhaar, bank account details, and income certificate before the deadline announced each academic year. ## Institutional Scholarships The merit scholarship covers full tuition fees for the top student of each branch every semester. Students with a CGPA above 9.0 and 100 percent attendance receive a Rs. 10,000 cash award each semester. The merit-cum-means scholarship covers 50 percent of the tuition fee for students with family income below Rs. 2.5 lakh per year and a CGPA above 8.0. Sports scholarships of Rs. 15,000

title: Scholarship Details
content: merit-cum-means scholarship covers 50 percent of the tuition fee for students with family income below Rs. 2.5 lakh per year and a CGPA above 8.0. Sports scholarships of Rs. 15,000 per year are given to students representing the college at state or national level competitions. ## Need-Based Financial Aid Students facing financial hardship can apply for the student emergency fund through the Student Welfare Office. The fund provides one-time assistance up to Rs. 25,000 for medical emergencies, hostel dues, or academic fees. Applications are reviewed by the welfare committee within two weeks and require a recommendation letter from the class mentor. ## Application Process Scholarship applications open every year in August. Students fill the online application form, upload supporting documents such as marksheets, income certificates, category certificates, and bank passbook details. The scholarship committee verifies documents and releases the beneficiary

title: Scholarship Details
content: August. Students fill the online application form, upload supporting documents such as marksheets, income certificates, category certificates, and bank passbook details. The scholarship committee verifies documents and releases the beneficiary list. Disbursement happens directly to the student bank account through the Direct Benefit Transfer system. ## Renewal Rules Scholarships are renewed every year based on academic performance. Students must maintain a minimum CGPA of 6.5 and clear all backlogs to continue receiving scholarship benefits. Scholarship benefits are discontinued if a student fails two consecutive semesters or is found to have submitted false information in the application.
